item.title: 'Racism and Xenophobia have no place': Irish embassy condemns violence against Indians; announces their deputy PM will meet Indian diaspora
item.description: The Ireland embassy in India has strongly condemned the violent attacks against Indian citizens, emphasizing that racism and xenophobia are unacceptable. Ireland's deputy prime minister will meet with Indian community representatives to address concerns.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Emory University shooting: Suspect killed, officer injured — what we know so far
item.description: An active shooter incident near Emory University and the CDC in Atlanta resulted in the deaths of the shooter and a police officer. Gunfire erupted near the Emory Point CVS, impacting nearby buildings, including the CDC. Georgia's governor linked the incident to another recent shooting, praising first responders and offering prayers for those affected.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Trump-Putin summit: Meeting set for next Friday in Alaska; to discuss ending Ukraine war
item.description: President Donald Trump announced a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Alaska on August 15, 2025, to discuss ending the ongoing war in Ukraine. This marks Putin's first visit to the US in a decade, signaling a potential shift in diplomatic efforts. Trump expressed optimism about brokering a peace deal, despite previous failed talks between Moscow and Kyiv.

item.title: Australia: Mushroom murderer accused of poisoning husband
item.description: Erin Patterson, already convicted of fatally poisoning three in-laws with mushrooms, faced accusations of also attempting to murder her husband, Simon Patterson. Simon testified about multiple instances of illness following meals prepared by Erin, including a chicken korma curry, leading him to suspect poisoning.

item.title: German court rejects deported Yazidi family's return
item.description: An emergency appeal by a Yazidi family deported to Iraq has been rejected by the Potsdam Administrative Court, stirring controversy. The family's removal, part of a larger deportation, occurred despite concerns raised by Brandenburg officials. Critics argue the deportation disregards Germany's recognition of the Yazidi genocide by IS.

item.title: 'No plans to recognize Palestine as state': JD Vance says after UK talks
item.description: US Vice President JD Vance stated that Washington has no plans to recognize Palestine as a state, citing the absence of a functional government. This contrasts with the UK's intention to recognize Palestine by September if a Gaza ceasefire isn't achieved.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Random Musing: The multi-pronged approach to dealing with Donald Trump's tariffs
item.description: ​ India has always refused to bow to foreign powers, even when we were a far poorer economy. We have weathered Persians, Mughals, Mongols, Brits, and the launch of the ₹2,000 note. We can manage one ex-reality-TV-host-turned-president with a spray tan. The correct procedure is a multi-pronged approach unleashing all spheres of society: political, judicial, civil, and the particularly uncivil.
item.dc:creator: Nirmalya Dutta

item.title: UAE launches national programme to train Emiratis in space mission design and satellite engineering
item.description: The UAE Space Agency’s National Space Academy has partnered with EDGE Group to launch a 10-week Space Mission and Satellite Engineering Programme, aimed at training Emirati talent in satellite systems and mission design. Delivered with EDGE subsidiaries BEACON RED and FADA, the programme marks the Academy’s fourth cohort, advancing the UAE’s long-term vision for sovereign space capabilities.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'PM Modi can't, shouldn't bend knee to Donald Trump': US tariffs on India draws rare bipartisan concern in US - watch
item.description: US President Trump's tariff war against India has sparked bipartisan concern in the US. Kurt Campbell warned that US-India ties are at risk, advising Modi not to yield to Trump. Mike Pence criticized tariffs for burdening American companies and consumers, advocating free trade.
item.dc:creator: TOI News Desk

item.title: 'Enormous mistake': What Trump's former NSA John Bolton said on India tariff
item.description: "The White House seems headed toward more-lenient treatment for Beijing on tariff rates and other metrics than it imposed on New Delhi. If so, it will be a potentially enormous mistake. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has suggested that China’s Aug. 12 deadline could be extended if negotiations looked promising," Trump's former NSA John Bolton wrote.
